title: Ancient Trees in Brazil: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Brazil's most famous tree isn't old, it's enormous: one cashew spread across 8,500 square metres. Three cities mapped, 8 trees.
intro: Brazil's most famous tree by international record is not its oldest. The Cajueiro de Pirangi, a single cashew whose branches root wherever they touch the ground, has spread across roughly 8,500 square metres near Natal and held the Guinness record for the largest cashew tree since 1994, at the modest age of about 138. The genuinely old trees keep quieter company: O Patriarca, a jequitiba-rosa in the cerrado of Vassununga State Park, is called the country's oldest by a press that cannot agree whether that means 600 years or more than 3,000. Rio de Janeiro supplies the range in between, a sumauma linked to Tom Jobim, a fig tree with a disputed two centuries behind it, a baobab that arrived on ships from Africa long before anyone thought to write its age down. Three cities mapped so far, eight trees, from a single record-holding cashew to a rainforest giant nobody can date.
